title: Understanding Bluff and Fold in Texas Hold'em
summaryJa: ポーカーの「ブラフ」と「フォールド」は基本的な戦略用語です。ブラフは弱いハンドで強いふりをすること、フォールドは手札を降りることを意味します。
segments: Texas Hold'em is a popular card game. Players try to win money by making the best hand or by tricking other players.
Two important words in this game are bluff and fold. Learning these words helps you understand how people play poker.
A bluff is when a player makes a bet even though their cards are not very good. The player hopes other players think they have a strong hand.
For example, imagine you have two low cards. The community cards on the table are not good for you either.
But you bet a lot of money anyway. You want the other players to think you have a strong hand and make them leave the game.
This is a bluff. Fold means to leave the game and stop playing your hand.
When you fold, you give up your chance to win the pot. The pot is all the money players put into the middle of the table.
For example, another player bets a lot of money. You look at your cards and think they are not good enough to win.
You decide to fold. You put your cards face down.
Now you cannot win this round. Another player might win the pot instead.
Bluff and fold are connected. A good bluff makes other players fold.
They think you have a strong hand, so they fold their cards and leave. Then you win the pot without showing your cards.
Understanding these two words is the first step to playing better poker.
